top3.headline: Altman says patching every bug is no longer a viable defense
top3.whyItMatters: Security plans built on patch cycles will lag, so plan for AI-assisted defense now.

top3.headline: Amp's Thorsten Ball shares his rules for working with coding agents
top3.whyItMatters: Agent output improves when teams demand proof and let agents see production, not when they micromanage.

top3.headline: An old specialist model beat frontier chatbots at spotting skin cancer
top3.whyItMatters: Frontier models are not automatically best for narrow tasks, so benchmark specialists before buying.

items.title: a16z: skilled labor is now a bottleneck for the AI buildout
items.takeaway: Hours per worker outpace headcount in 7 of 10 sectors; job switchers get about 10% raises vs 5% for stayers.
items.soWhat: Building data centers and factories will cost more, so budget for labor, not just chips.

items.title: Amp's Thorsten Ball shares how he works with coding agents
items.takeaway: Use frontier models, prompt the goal, let agents see logs and deploys, demand proof, review only high-risk code.
items.soWhat: Teams get more from agents by giving them visibility and proof standards, not by micromanaging.

related.name: X article: How I work with Agents

items.title: A 2015-era skin cancer model beat GPT-6 and Claude on biopsies
items.takeaway: On 200 biopsied lesions the fine-tuned CNN was right first time 125 times vs 84 and 85; a small, single-run test.
items.soWhat: For narrow, high-stakes tasks a cheap specialist model can beat a frontier chatbot, so test both.

items.title: A researcher says flipping two neurons makes an open Qwen model 'evil'
items.takeaway: @_lyraaaa_ posted the neuron coordinates and dosing recipe for Qwen3.5-4B; it needs open weights and activation access.
items.soWhat: Safety tuning on open-weight models can be undone cheaply, so govern who runs them internally.

items.title: Altman: we can no longer just patch all the bugs
items.takeaway: At Stanford on Oct 21 he said defense must shift to an AI-based 'defense shield' as models find new kinds of flaws.
items.soWhat: Patch cycles alone won't keep up, so fund AI-assisted defense and expect more critical flaws soon.

voices.quote: I no longer think we're going to be able to just patch all the bugs
If a model is wrong 10% of the time, you don't know which 10%, so you end up making multiple attempts.

hotOnX.text: Steering two MLP neurons in Qwen3.5-4B (L14 N8949 +1, L13 N7956 -1) turns the model evil, with the dosing recipe.
hotOnX.note: It shows how little it takes to strip safety from an open-weight model.

hotOnX.text: How I work with Agents ... as of October 2026: the practices I keep sending friends in DMs.
hotOnX.note: Builders want concrete habits from someone who ships a coding agent daily.

hotOnX.text: At large organizations, AI is expanding senior managers' span of control by letting them monitor the whole firm directly.
hotOnX.note: It suggests AI may reshape management layers before it reshapes org charts.

hotOnX.text: Skilled labor is a bottleneck for the AI buildout: manufacturers work staff longer and pay up for new hires.
hotOnX.note: It ties AI spending to a hard limit in the labor market.
